L26:   * # Forecasting LLM-enabled Biorisk and the Efficacy of Safeguards

L28: Forecasting LLM-enabled Biorisk and the Efficacy of Safeguards
L29: 
L30: This forecasting study on biological risks from large language models (LLMs) examined expert views on AI-enabled biosecurity threats. The study saw 46 biosecurity and biology experts, along with 22 superforecasters, predict how advancing LLM capabilities might increase the risk of a human-caused epidemic.

L52: Contents
L53: Bridget Williams^{1*}, Luca Righetti^{2}, Josh Rosenberg^{1}, Rebecca Ceppas de Castro^{1}, Otto Kuusela^{1}, Rhiannon Britt^{1}, Emily Soice^{3}, Alvaro Morales^{3}, Jon Sanders^{3}, Seth Donoughe^{3}, James Black^{4}, Ezra Karger^{1,5}, Philip E. Tetlock^{1,6}
L54: ## Abstract
L55: Capabilities of large language models (LLMs) on several biological benchmarks have prompted excitement about their usefulness for beneficial research, but also concern about potential biosecurity risks. We recruited 46 subject-matter experts in biology and biosecurity, and 22 generalist forecasters to estimate the risks of growing LLM capabilities. The median expert predicted a 0.3% baseline annual risk of a human-caused epidemic that causes 100,000 deaths.
L56: This estimate then rose to 1.5% conditional on several hypothetical LLM capabilities, including matching the performance of a top-performing team of virologists on a virology troubleshooting test. Given this finding, we conducted a baselining study and found that LLMs have already crossed this performance threshold. The median respondent thought that this would not happen until after 2030.
L57: More encouragingly, experts reduced their risk forecast close to baseline (0.4%) conditional on the adoption of LLM safeguards and mandatory nucleic acid screening.

L66: ## Main
L67: 
L68: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong improvements in biological capabilities and now outperform PhD-level experts on a variety of biology benchmarks.^{cite15†1 } Similarly, LLMs have shown early promise in providing scientific tutoring^{cite16†2 } and assisting with the conduct of scientific research.^{cite17†3 } While there are still clear limitations to how useful LLMs can be in science,^{cite18†4 } there is a clear trend that new models are more capable than their predecessors.
L69: Numerous observers—including leaders of frontier AI companies—recognize both the benefits and risks that such capabilities could bring in the near future.^{cite19†5 } OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Anthropic have all released policies to prevent LLM misuse of biology and run capability evaluations on new models ahead of their commercial deployment.^{cite20†6 } Recently, Anthropic announced that it provisionally implemented a stronger security standard for its latest model release, since it could not rule out that it might significantly assist with CBRN-weapons-related tasks of concern.^{cite21†7 } OpenAI has announced that it is preparing similar mitigations.^{cite22†8 } However, it is still unclear which empirical evaluation results would indicate that LLMs present a meaningful increase in risk.^{cite23†9 } It is also unclear what sorts of mitigation measures would then be most helpful in reducing such risk while preserving the power of the models to advance scientific work.
L70: Forecasting the probability of biological threats is challenging due to the rarity of such events and the complex interplay of technical, social, and political factors involved.^{cite24†10 } Previous surveys have found a wide range of views.
L71: In a 2005 study of 83 nonproliferation and national security experts, the median respondent gave a 10% probability of a major biological weapons attack within 5 years, with individual responses ranging from 0% to more than 80%.^{cite25†11 } A 2009 survey of biological scientists found a mean forecast of roughly 50% probability of a bioterrorist within 5 years.^{cite26†12 } Similarly, a 2015 survey of relevant experts found a mean forecast of roughly 50% probability of a biological weapons attack causing more than 100 cases of illness within 10 years.^{cite27†13 }
